Key risks include competition from marketplaces and quick commerce, inventory and discounting pressure, and the cost of making overseas operations and acquired brands sustainably profitable.

BEML Limited is a Government of India-owned engineering company that manufactures equipment for mining, construction, railways, metro systems and defence. Its products include earthmoving machinery, railway and metro coaches, trainsets, specialised defence vehicles and heavy engineering equipment.

GNG Electronics Limited is an Indian information and communication technology (ICT) refurbishment company operating under the Electronics Bazaar brand. It specialises in sourcing, refurbishing and selling pre-owned laptops, desktops, workstations and other IT devices, alongside distribution and after-sales services. Its business model extends the useful life of electronic equipment, making technology more affordable while reducing electronic waste. Growth drivers: Increasing demand for affordable computing devices, growing corporate IT asset-disposal and buyback requirements, expansion of refurbished electronics in international markets, and rising adoption of circular-economy practices.

Aeroflex Industries Limited manufactures stainless-steel flexible hoses, hose assemblies and engineered flow solutions used in data centres, oil and gas, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, power and industrial applications, exporting to more than 90 countries. Growth drivers: Rising demand for liquid-cooling systems in AI data centres. Threat : If AI is bubble and AI companies can't generate revenues as per investments.

Power Mech Projects Limited is an Indian engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company providing power-plant erection, testing, commissioning and operations and maintenance (O&M) services, alongside civil infrastructure, industrial construction and mining services. Growth drivers: Entry in civil work of Nuclear Power Plannts and recent Privatisation of Nuclear space via SHANTI BILL can give boost to more demand for civil projects for the company.

Steel Strips Wheels manufactures steel and alloy wheels for passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles, tractors and off-highway vehicles, supplying Indian and international automotive manufacturers. Growth drivers: Rising vehicle production, premiumisation of SUVs and electric vehicles, and increasing demand for lightweight aluminium alloy wheels are key opportunities.

KPI Green Energy Limited is an Indian renewable energy company engaged in developing, owning and operating solar, wind and hybrid power projects, serving both corporate customers through its Captive Power Producer (CPP) business and utilities through its Independent Power Producer (IPP) business. Growth drivers: India’s renewable-energy targets, rising corporate demand for clean electricity, expansion into wind-solar hybrid projects and battery energy storage, and increasing recurring income from commissioned power assets. Key threats: High capital expenditure and debt, rising interest and depreciation costs, project delays, land and transmission constraints, and dependence on timely customer payments.

JBM Auto supplies vehicle components, assemblies and manufacturing tools to automakers, while expanding into electric buses supported by battery systems, charging infrastructure and fleet operations. Its growth opportunity lies in India’s shift towards electric public transport and demand from private bus operators, alongside its established components business. Key risks include funding-intensive bus contracts, deployment and payment delays, and rising input costs on fixed-price orders; its components business also remains exposed to automobile demand cycles.

Rentomojo rents furniture and home appliances through subscriptions, earning recurring income by refurbishing and renting products across multiple customers. It is expanding its city coverage and experience stores, targeting consumers who want furnished homes without large upfront purchases. Urban migration, frequent relocation and demand for flexible living offer long-term opportunities. Profitability depends on keeping assets rented and controlling delivery, repair and refurbishment costs; key risks include idle inventory, customer defaults, early cancellations and faster-than-expected product wear.

Deep Industries provides specialised oil and gas field services, including natural gas compression and processing, drilling rigs, workover rigs and integrated project management. Growth drivers: Rising domestic oil and gas exploration, demand for outsourced field services, and expansion into offshore operations following its acquisition of Dolphin Offshore. The company is also exploring higher-capacity drilling rigs to capture larger contracts. Key threats: Dependence on a limited number of clients, delays in procuring specialised equipment, shortage of skilled personnel, and fluctuations in oil and gas industry investment.
AI-first digital engineering and IT services company. Stock has faced significant de-rating amid sector challenges because of AI-concerns.

Wakefit Innovations sells mattresses, furniture and home furnishings through its website, marketplaces and physical stores, with in-house manufacturing supporting cost and quality control. It is expanding its store network and furniture range to become a broader home-products brand. Rising spending on homes and a shift from unbranded to organised products offer long-term opportunities. Key risks include dependence on mattress sales, intense price competition, bulky-product delivery and return costs, and the challenge of making new stores profitable.
One of India’s Big IT firms. AI revenue ~$1 bn+ (around 5.5% of total); High US depedence. AI disruption potentially reducing traditional services demand and pricing.

Kirloskar Pneumatic Company Limited is an Indian industrial engineering company that manufactures air and gas compressors, refrigeration systems, process gas solutions and mechanical power transmission equipment. Its products serve industries such as oil and gas, manufacturing, chemicals, infrastructure, railways, food processing and power generation.

MosChip Technologies Limited is a semiconductor and product engineering company providing chip design, ASIC design and development, embedded systems, VLSI and product engineering services to customers across industries. Growth drivers: Rising global semiconductor demand, India’s semiconductor-design initiatives, increasing outsourcing of chip development, and demand for connected devices, automotive electronics and high-performance computing. Its capabilities across the semiconductor design cycle and expansion of engineering services provide opportunities to win larger projects.

VST Tillers Tractors specialises in power tillers and compact tractors suited to small farms, orchards and vineyards. It is broadening its small-farm machinery range, expanding into higher-powered tractors through VST Zetor and developing overseas markets for its compact models. Farm-labour shortages and demand for affordable mechanisation offer long-term growth opportunities. Key risks include monsoon-dependent farm incomes, delays in government subsidies that influence equipment purchases, and competition as it moves beyond its established niche.

Stock_About: VST Industries manufactures cigarettes under brands such as Total, Editions and Charms, alongside selling unmanufactured tobacco. Historically focused on lower-priced cigarettes, it is expanding into mid-premium products through Total and Editions to capture higher-value demand. Wider distribution and an improved product mix offer growth opportunities, but its concentrated tobacco exposure leaves it sensitive to taxation, tighter regulation and illicit cigarettes. Rising tobacco-leaf costs and limited pricing power in the value segment can also pressure profitability.
Hindustan Oil Exploration Company (HOEC) is a private-sector oil and gas exploration and production company.

Asian Energy Services provides oilfield services, including seismic data acquisition, drilling, production enhancement and integrated field management, alongside mineral and energy infrastructure services. Growth drivers: A ₹865 crore integrated field-management contract with Vedanta, a ₹459 crore coal-handling project for Mahanadi Coalfields, and the acquisition of Kuiper Group, expanding its international footprint. The proposed merger with Oilmax Energy, sanctioned by NCLT in September 2026, could create a more integrated energy platform. Key threats: Project execution delays, working-capital requirements, integration risks and dependence on large contracts. Sustained growth depends on converting its expanded order book into profitable cash flows.

Turtlemint Fintech Solutions distributes insurance through a network of local advisers equipped with digital tools to compare, sell and service policies, earning commissions from insurers. Low insurance penetration and the digitisation of adviser-led sales offer long-term growth opportunities. Key risks include heavy reliance on motor insurance, changes to commission rules, dependence on insurer relationships and the cost of attracting and retaining productive advisers.

One MobiKwik Systems combines wallet and UPI payments with Zaakpay’s merchant payment gateway and distribution of credit and investment products. It is expanding merchant services and preparing to enter direct lending through its financial-services subsidiary. Key challenges include intense payments competition, regulatory compliance and converting its user base into sustainably profitable customers.

Stock_Name: Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets

Stock_About: Global IT services, consulting, and business process outsourcing company. AI-driven productivity compressing traditional services pricing and demand. Soft discretionary spending, especially in America. Client concentration and slower organic growth relative to some peers.

Digital-first discount broker and fintech platform; Less than 1% Market Share; Pivoting to AI/research to differentiate (plans for ChatGPT integration), but faces scale and profitability challenges in a crowded market.

SpiceJet Limited is an Indian low-cost airline providing domestic and international passenger services, cargo transportation and related aviation services. The company is attempting to rebuild its fleet, restore grounded aircraft and improve its financial position after years of losses and operational challenges. Key threats: Severe financial stress, high lease and fuel costs, rupee depreciation, aircraft groundings, delayed salaries, legal disputes with lessors and intense competition from IndiGo and other airlines.

Atul Auto manufactures passenger and cargo three-wheelers for local transport and last-mile deliveries, supported by vehicle financing through Khushbu Auto Finance. It is expanding its electric range through Atul Greentech and partnerships for rapid charging and battery swapping. Growing delivery demand and the shift towards lower-running-cost electric three-wheelers offer opportunities, but also intensify competition from established manufacturers and EV entrants. Key risks include customers’ access to finance, changing EV incentives and the cost of keeping pace with battery technology.

Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Limited is an Indian multinational pharmaceutical company that develops, manufactures and markets generic medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), biosimilars and specialty medicines. It serves patients and healthcare providers across India and international markets, with a focus on affordable treatments, complex generics and selected therapeutic areas.
